findings.summary: Runtime lane's first real artifact set exists and self-reports VERDICT PASS on all six frozen gates (P1.2 no-silent-exec-after-FAIL, P1.3 handoff materialized valid, P1.6 stale discrimination host✓url✓elem✗, P2.1 detection overhead D=236.343ms ≤ 500ms, P2.2 cell-A wall ratio 1.1293 ≤ 3×, P2.3 fallback neutrality 4 vs 4 novel actions ≤ +2). Built per CTO-4 FIRST COMMIT order: (1) COST_EVENT pack field-for-field identical to Product's frozen D8 envelope under dual-name rule spider.*/pb001.*; (2) capsule/v0+plan/v0 schemas with stdlib validator and fixture-covered type traps; (3) pure-stdlib agent-facing loop resolve→default-deny applicability→ONE executor→cheap verify→materialized handoff-to-caller→report with explicit ABSTAIN and retrieval_version rv0:e22a766b289c4fdbbf99f289c9c2d81d pinning bytes+matcher+thresholds; (4) two CANDIDATE capsules derived programmatically (no hand-phrased intent text) from accepted Graph store dump; (5) two-cell pilot + live confirm vs scripted zero-provider baseline, 58/58 tests incl. foreign-executor plan-consumability parity. ALL OF THIS IS DURABLE_UNAUDITED — the independent audit never ran.

Honest economics negative (ledger finding C1): whole-task exact-repeat inheritance does NOT beat a strong zero-provider scripted baseline on T1 login — both arms 4 actions, 100% success, SPIDER pays ≈+29% wall overhead (cell-A medians 1475.7ms vs 1306.8ms; ≈+380ms incl. 236ms retrieval/applicability detection D) for ZERO action savings (inherited=[4,4,4] equals baseline actions). Work-compression from replay-style inheritance is not demonstrated at this scale; per prereg claims_license, NO work-compression claim is licensed this cycle (scripted arms, n=2 capsules, zero provider tokens). Counterpoint (descriptive only): localized inheritance on T2 pagination succeeded with 1 inherited action where the baseline failed entirely (mirror 3/3 vs 0/3; live baseline 30-action overshoot vs SPIDER 1 action success) — caveated as partially fixture-bound because the mirror lacks /tag/../page/N surfaces.

ROOT CAUSE of run failure — control-plane contradiction between the CTO charter and the lane scope gate: docs/CTO_TO_RUNTIME.md (lab/cto, CTO-4 council pass) FIRST COMMIT items 1–2 explicitly order building directives/COST_EVENT.md + spider.cost_event.v0 JSON Schema + capsule/v0+plan/v0 schemas ('next lane commit must produce the COST_EVENT pack or a schema/validator/benchmark artifact — not workflow plumbing'), but the 'Enforce Runtime scope' allowlist in runtime-loop.yml line 140 (byte-identical to what ran; unchanged since the workflow was created at 7669dcd) permits only runtime/, tests/runtime/, results/runtime/, reports/runtime/, data/manifests/runtime/, docs/RUNTIME_LEDGER.md, docs/NEXT_RUNTIME.md, state/runtime_loop.json, directives/RUNTIME.md. The team followed the charter, and after ~64 minutes of green work the gate flagged exactly BAD='directives/COST_EVENT.md' + 'schemas/' and exited 1 → run conclusion=failure, Auditor/Director skipped, lab/runtime unchanged. This is mechanism-DISTINCT from the porcelain false-positive family (CF-2026-08-25-08): here the violation is real, but mandated by another control-plane document. Same genus, third instance: write-scope gates killing completed lane work. The allowlist is STILL stale at current main HEAD, so the next scheduled Runtime run will fail identically even though the artifacts now exist on the cycle branch.
